__inputs.name: DS_INFINITY
__inputs.label: Estate API (Infinity)
__inputs.description: Infinity data source whose base URL points at the estate relationship API (or the mock). Queries use URLs relative to it.

description: Interactive view of the infrastructure estate (datacenters, zones, subnets, firewalls, racks, ESXi, bare metal, VMs, OpenShift clusters, nodes, namespaces, pods) read from the relationship API. Pick a root object, a depth and a direction; one traversal call feeds every panel.

options.content: **Root** is where the walk starts, **Depth** how many relationship hops to follow, **Direction** which way: *down* = what the root contains or provides, *up* = what the root depends on, *both* = everything near it. Every panel below is a different view of the **same single API call** (`/traverse`). Double-click a node in the topology, or use *make root* in its details, to re-centre the whole dashboard on it.

panels.title: Objects in view, by type
panels.description: Count of each object type returned by the traversal. Hide/show types in the topology legend; this count is unaffected.

panels.title: OpenShift clusters reached
panels.description: Distinct clusters among the OpenShift nodes in view. With a subnet or host as root this answers: how many clusters run on it?

panels.title: Physical cores in view
panels.description: Sum of CPU cores over the ESXi and bare-metal hosts in view: the hardware footprint under the current root.

panels.title: Topology
panels.description: Layered map of everything the traversal returned: containers on top, what they contain below. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, click for details, double-click to make a node the root. Source: grafana/estate/panel/.

options.html:
No objects. The source panel returned no rows for this root.
Click a node for its details and relations. Double-click (or "make root") to re-centre the whole dashboard on it. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, click a legend chip to hide a type.

panels.title: Objects in view
panels.description: SOURCE PANEL: the only panel that calls the API (two queries against /traverse: nodes and edges). Every other panel reads these rows through the built-in Dashboard data source. Use the column filters (funnel icons) to answer granular questions, e.g. type = vm to see every VM and its OS.

panels.title: Host utilisation (CPU, memory)
panels.description: ESXi and bare-metal hosts in view, from the same rows. Each bar is one host and one measure (the display-name override reads the host name from the row). Colour thresholds: 70% warning, 85% critical.

panels.title: Topology (built-in Node Graph, no custom code)
panels.description: The same nodes and edges in Grafana's stock Node Graph panel. It reads fixed field names (id, title, subtitle, mainstat, detail__*), so the source queries emit those as extra alias columns. Fine for a few hundred objects; the custom panel above scales and explains better.

list.name: root
list.label: Root
list.description: Where the relationship walk starts. Any object can be a root; this list offers the usual starting points.

list.name: depth
list.label: Depth (hops)
list.description: How many relationship hops to follow from the root. 'all' walks to the end.

list.name: direction
list.label: Direction
list.description: down: what the root contains or provides. up: what the root depends on. both: everything near it (fans out quickly).
